_doc: Slugs whose svek DOT differs from the oracle's ONLY in edge DIRECTION -- the orientation of one or more edges is reversed relative to upstream's own Link order. Until 2026-08-11 the structural comparison was entirely orientation-blind: `tests/oracle/svek-dot.ts#structurallyEqual` is a conjunction of node/edge counts, `degreeSequence` (which increments BOTH endpoints and sorts, i.e. UNDIRECTED), and sorted multisets of minlens/shapes/ports/cluster-sizes plus three scalar graph attrs -- reversing `a -> b` to `b -> a` left every one of them invariant. That is how M7 (the decor-driven endpoint swap, fixed at B6) survived in 116 of 722 class fixtures while they all scored EQUAL. B31 added `directionOk`, a sorted `in:out` degree multiset, and these slugs are what it surfaced -- pre-existing defects, NOT regressions introduced by the gate. A listed slug is NOT skipped: `class-dot-parity.test.ts` asserts it fails `directionOk` and NOTHING else, so every other structural check stays live for it. Remove a slug the moment its orientation is fixed; the list is shrink-only. Cause is NOT yet attributed -- see plans/object-close/ledger.md B33 for the audit item. A sampled fixture (befasi-62-vimu310) shows the candidate's out-degrees collapsed into a hub (5:0, 7:0) where the oracle has none, so at least some of these are edges emitted from a single source that upstream emits per-pair. T1/B33 (2026-08-11) removed 28 of the original 32: the dominant cause was `dotEdgeRunsReversed` inferring orientation by comparing `idEntity1FullId` against `from`/`to`, which endpoint resolution rewrites, so every namespace/package fixture reported "not reversed" and returned early. Replaced by the parse-time `Relationship.dotEdgeReversed` flag.
